Note. For each outcome, the six focal predictors were set to their favorable, neutral, or unfavorable values and all other predictors held at the sample reference. Continuous predictors: neutral, the sample median; favorable and unfavorable, the 10th and 90th percentiles, oriented by the direction of the SHAP dependence (BMI uses clinical bands). Categorical predictors: neutral, the modal category; favorable and unfavorable, the categories with the most and least healthy mean SHAP contribution among categories with at least 30 observations. Predictions are from the cross-sectional model on the age-residualized scale, where zero is the sample average for a given age; 95% CIs are percentiles of 200 bootstrap refits with hyperparameters fixed, and omit model-selection variance. Sample percentile, the position of the prediction in the observed outcome distribution. Exploratory and model-implied, not causal; the allostatic-load drinking setting follows the model's direction and is not a recommendation.
